_comment: What we have actually run, not what we recommend. Models age in weeks and this file is
fetched at runtime for that reason: a name compiled into the installer would still be
advertised long after it stopped being a sensible choice, and the installer does not
update itself.
Rules for adding a line here:
- only models someone on the project has actually run the instruction suite against
- 'note' says what was observed, in one sentence, with no superlative
- never a ranking: the suite is a heuristic on free text and the machine matters as much
as the model. The person testing decides; this only tells them where to start.
- NEVER pick or rank by language. Sorting by 'good at Japanese' would break the rule the
whole project is built on: every part of it stays language-agnostic.
'pull' is what makes a model offerable for download. An entry without it is a note only —
which is right for a family name like 'gemma' that matches many things, and for anything we
would not put in front of someone as a starting point.
TAGS ARE PINNED TO A VERSION, NEVER 'latest'. A moving tag makes every figure below a lie
the day it moves, and the reader has no way of knowing which day that was.
'min_vram_gb' is the card size below which the model runs on the processor instead, which
means minutes per line rather than seconds. It filters the offer; it never hides the list.
⚠ It is NOT the download size, and the two differ wildly in BOTH directions: gemma4:e4b
downloads 9.6 GB and ran here in 3.0, qwen3:8b downloads 5.2 GB and took 9.3. Measured with
the model tester where we could; where we could not, it is an estimate and the note says so.
'languages' is the PUBLISHER'S claim, never our measurement — we have verified none of them.
Two numbers when they give two: a model tuned for 35 languages that merely saw 140 in
training is not the same promise, and the difference matters to whoever falls in the gap.
⚠ It stays a COUNT. Recording WHICH languages, and filtering the offer by what somebody is
translating into, is the one thing this project does nowhere.

models.note: What the mod is developed against. Follows the instruction suite in full, including the experimental source-language rule.
Kept the placeholders and answered with the translation alone. Ran in 3.0 GB of video memory here — a third of what its download suggests, and half the reference model.
Translation-specialised and light enough for a small card. Drops a placeholder sitting at the very end of a line.
Kept the placeholders and answered with the translation alone, but needed 9.3 GB of video memory here — well beyond what its 5.2 GB download suggests, and beyond an 8 GB card.
Translation-specialised. The larger build was not better here than the small one.

A whole family rather than one model, so no size or figure is given here. Gemma has no separate system turn — it is merged into the conversation, which makes it more sensitive to how instructions are phrased.

Reasons before answering, so every line costs noticeably more time. Not offered for download either: the smaller build is a 14 GB download and the other 65 GB, both beyond the cards this tool is aimed at.
